recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit historical release archives. If a future rendered current operation page reintroduces 'official URL' wording for operation definitions, trace the renderer that emits that current page rather than changing OperationDefinition canonical url values.
issue_request: FHIR-20194 was a Published FHIR-core change request with Persuasive with Modification resolution asking that operation definition pages say canonical URL rather than official URL for OperationDefinition canonical identifiers.
initial_application: Git commit 6b0a5cd0facd39e897a6f470f78192b5a79150f2 explicitly applied FHIR-20194 by changing tools/templates/template-profile.html from 'The official URL for this profile is:' to 'The canonical URL for this profile is:'. Current blame for that active template line points to the FHIR-20194 commit.
additional_context: OperationDefinition remains an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and current operation definition XML sources carry canonical url elements. Active-source searches excluding release-history, publish, temp, and tmp artifacts found no 'official URL for this operation definition' wording and no remaining 'official URL for this profile' wording. Historical tools/history archives still preserve old release text and were intentionally not edited. Community searches found no direct FHIR-20194 Zulip or Confluence discussion and no conflicting related Jira decision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current source already reflects the approved terminology, so an empty no-change audit commit was published.
